blocks.text: It is an electric circuit. The Wheatstone bridge circuit shown in Fig. 9.30 consists of four resistances R₁, R₂, R₃ and R₄ connected in such a way so as to form a mesh ABCDA. A battery is connected between points A and C. A sensitive galvanometer of resistance R_g is connected between points B and D. If the switch S is closed, a current will flow through the galvanometer. We have to determine the condition under which no current flows through the galvanometer even after the switch is closed. For this purpose, we analyse this circuit using Kirchhoff's second rule. We consider two loops ABDA and BCDB and assume anticlockwise loop currents I₁ and I₂ through the loops respectively. The Kirchhoff's second rule as applied to loop ABDA gives:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Eqs. 9.48 to 9.50 are not right: −I₁R₁ = I₁R₃ would need a negative resistance, and Eq. 9.50 is misprinted (IR₁₁, IR₁₃). The loop equations leave out the battery's loop current (I₃ in Fig. 9.30), which also flows through R₃ and R₄. When no current flows through the galvanometer, one current I flows through R₁ and R₂ and another current I′ through R₃ and R₄, and B and D are at the same potential, so IR₁ = I′R₃ and IR₂ = I′R₄. Dividing gives R₁/R₂ = R₃/R₄, the book's result (Eq. 9.51), which is right.

blocks.title: Point to ponder!
blocks.text: Why is a three pin plug used in some electric appliances?

Thus, whenever the condition of Eq. 9.51 is satisfied, no current flows through the galvanometer and it shows no deflection, or conversely when the galvanometer in the Wheatstone bridge circuit shows no deflection, Eq. 9.51 is satisfied. If we connect three resistances R₁, R₂ and R₃ of known adjustable values and a fourth resistance R₄ of unknown value and the resistances R₁, R₂ and R₃ are so adjusted that the galvanometer shows no deflection, then from the known resistances R₁, R₂ and R₃, the unknown resistance R₄ can be determined by using Eq. 9.49.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Eq. 9.49 is an intermediate step. The balance condition is Eq. 9.51, R₁/R₂ = R₃/R₄, which gives R₄ = R₂R₃/R₁.
